outputs.exact_statement:
For every fixed real $q>4$, there is a deterministic constant $c(q)\in(0,\infty)$ such that, as $n\to\infty$ through all positive integers, $$\big(V(M_n),c(q)n^{-1/2}d_n,\mu_n\big)
 \ \Longrightarrow\ (\mathcal T_e,d_e,\mu_e)$$ in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology on compact metric probability spaces modulo measure-preserving isometry.

Feed a finite word an arbitrary older list of burgers. Every match between two letters of the word is the same as when the word is read from an empty supply. The orders unfilled in the latter evaluation act on the older list in their original chronology, and the surviving burgers of the word remain above the surviving older burgers. In particular, finite words may be replaced by their reductions when concatenating them. Once a suffix has a surviving burger, its freshest survivor is unchanged by prepending further letters.

For every integer $n\ge0$, an independent word of length $2n$ satisfies $$\label{word:identity-equation}
 \mathbb P(\text{the word is empty-reducing})=a_nu^n.$$

The stopping time $J$ is almost surely finite, and $$\label{word:drift-equation}
 \mathbb EK\le\frac{1}{2p}<1.$$

There is $c>0$ such that, for all real $x<1$ sufficiently close to $1$, $$\sum_{n\ge1} n a_n u^n x^n\ge c(1-x)^{-1/2}.
 \label{ladder:coefficient-bound}$$

Let $(Z_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$ be iid, and let $Y_i$ be the translates of an integrable measurable function of the entire sequence $(Z_i)_{i\in\mathbb Z}$. Then the averages of $Y_i$ in each index direction converge almost surely to $\mathbb EY_0$. In particular, a shift-covariant set of boundaries having positive probability at boundary $0$ has positive limiting density in both directions. If $0$ belongs to this set, the last such boundary before $k$ is $k-o(k)$, and the first one after $-k$ is $-k+o(k)$.

Each fixed boundary has positive probability of being an $L$-cut and positive probability of being an $R$-cut, in the respective piece laws. Consequently both cut sets have positive limiting densities in both index directions.

Let a burger stack and an order word both have length $h$. Suppose that, for every $1\le k\le h$ and each type $a$, the number of fixed type-$a$ orders among the terminal $k$ orders is at most the number of type-$a$ burgers among the original bottom $k$ burgers. Then the greedy inventory rule matches all orders and leaves no burgers.

Almost surely, each burger type has frequency $1/2$ in the stationary $L$-output. The stationary $R$-output has almost-sure frequencies $(1-\rho)/2,(1-\rho)/2,\rho$ for the two fixed types and the flexible orders, respectively, for a deterministic $\rho>0$.*



*On the event that $0$ is an $L$-cut, let $B_a(h,k)$ count type-$a$ burgers among the bottom $k$ burgers of the reduction of the $h$ pieces starting at $0$, where $1\le k\le h$. Then, almost surely on this event, $$\lim_{k\to\infty}\sup_{h\ge k}
 \left|\frac{B_a(h,k)}k-\frac12\right|=0,
 \qquad a=1,2.
 \label{ladder:left-counts}$$ On the event that $0$ is an $R$-cut, let $C_a(h,k)$ count fixed orders of type $a$ among the terminal $k$ residual orders of the $h$ pieces ending at $0$. Then, almost surely on this event, $$\lim_{k\to\infty}\sup_{h\ge k}
 \left|\frac{C_a(h,k)}k-\frac{1-\rho}{2}\right|=0,
 \qquad a=1,2.
 \label{ladder:right-counts}$$

There is $\delta>0$, depending only on $p$, such that for every integer $h\ge1$ the seam interval formed by the backwards hit of $+h$ and the forwards hit of $-h$ reduces to the empty word with probability at least $\delta$.
The marked tree conditioned to have $N=2n+1$ nodes produces exactly the map marginal of [eq:finite-law]. Every such size is attainable.

We have $$\max_v H(v)=O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt N),\qquad
 \max_v W(v)=O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt N),\qquad
 \Delta_N=o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt N),
 \label{tree:degree-bound}$$ and $$\max_v|W(v)-\nu H(v)|=o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt N).
 \label{tree:walk-height-estimate}$$

As $N$ tends to infinity through odd integers, $$\pi_N:=\mathbb P(|\mathcal T|=N)
 \sim\frac{2}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}N^{-3/2}.
 \label{tree:size-probability}$$

For every fixed bounded measurable real label $b$, $$\max_{v\in\mathcal T_N}|B_b(v)-\mu_bH(v)|
 =o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt N).
 \label{tree:bounded-sums}$$

Let $b=b(k,i,A)$ be a fixed measurable label with $0\leq b\leq k$. Then $\mu_b<\infty$ and $$\max_{v\in\mathcal T_N}|B_b(v)-\mu_bH(v)|=o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt N),
 \qquad
 \max_{v\in\mathcal T_N}
 \left|B_b(v)-\frac{\mu_b}{\nu}W(v)\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt N).
 \label{tree:marked-sums}$$

If $j\leq j'$ and $v_*$ is the lowest common ancestor of $v_j,v_{j'}$, then $$W(v_*)\leq\min_{j\leq r\leq j'}W_r\leq W(v_*)+\Delta_N.
 \label{tree:lca-walk}$$

Let $w_*$ be the last common ancestor of two tree nodes $w,w'$. If $\Delta$ is the maximum offspring number, then $$\left|d_{M_n}\big(\pi(w),\pi(w')\big)
       -\big(G(w)+G(w')-2G(w_*)\big)\right|\le2\Delta.$$ The map $\pi$ from tree nodes to map vertices is onto.
The uniform probability measure on the $N-1=2n$ nonroot tree nodes, pushed forward by $\pi$, is exactly $\mu_n$.

Suppose a correspondence between compact metric probability spaces has distortion at most $\varepsilon>0$, and a coupling of their probability measures is supported on the correspondence. Their Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov distance is at most $\varepsilon$. If one marginal of that coupling differs from the desired measure by total variation at most $\eta$, the bound is $\varepsilon+\eta$.

purpose: Brownian continuum random tree limits of finite Fortuin–Kasteleyn maps above four

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive 0 <= h <= 5; every binary burger stack and ternary order word, with all consumed indices rechecked.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent exact relational replay using original timestamps and set maxima, plus fmpz terminal-demand/bottom-supply inequalities. Finite enumeration does not prove the unbounded lemma.
